item.title: Russian Blood and Treasure: The Ballooning Costs of Putin’s War
item.description: Russia has suffered approximately 1.4 million casualties and 450,000 fatalities in Ukraine for only marginal territorial gains, according to new CSIS data. In addition, Ukraine has conducted deep strikes into Russian territory, including with AI-enabled drones.

item.title: Troubled Straits: Analyzing Trade Chokepoints in the South China Sea
item.description: This digital feature and dashboard offer groundbreaking data and insights into trade flows through critical chokepoints in the South China Sea.

item.title: States Weekly: July 1, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers July 1, 2026.

item.title: Europe Should Center Anti-Corruption in Its Democratic Resilience Efforts
item.description: Democracy is facing its biggest test in decades across Europe. To revive trust in institutions and ensure they deliver what citizens need, leaders must focus on anti-corruption efforts as the key to democratic resilience.

item.title: Troubled Straits: Analyzing Trade Chokepoints in the South China Sea
item.description: This CSIS brief offers groundbreaking insight into the value and types of goods flowing through eight different South China Sea chokepoints. The analysis reveals each country’s reliance on each chokepoint and challenges assumptions about their relative importance.

item.title: What a Fragile U.S.-Iran Ceasefire Means for Energy and Beyond
item.description: CSIS experts assess the implications of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire amid ongoing uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz and global energy markets.

item.title: Don’t Let the USMCA Drift Away
item.description: On July 1, North America’s trade pact comes up for review. The real risk isn’t collapse, but rather the slow, expensive erosion already underway.

item.title: Reflecting on U.S. Development Policy on the United States’ 250th Anniversary
item.description: As the United States marks its 250th anniversary, it faces a defining question: What role should development play in U.S. global leadership? This commentary explores why development remains central to U.S. strategy, trust, and leadership in an era of disruption.

item.title: What to Know About Chinese AI Models
item.description: Chinese AI models are rapidly closing the gap with U.S. frontier systems. This analysis examines what their growing capabilities, lower costs, and open-weight strategy mean for global AI competition and U.S. policy.

item.title: The United States Has Opted Not to Extend the USMCA
item.description: The United States declined to renew the USMCA for another 16 years, triggering a decade of annual reviews. But the deal did not collapse. It now faces a slower, costlier threat: prolonged uncertainty that stalls investment across North America.

item.title: Occupational Risk? Chinese Presence Surges at Scarborough Shoal
item.description: CCG presence at Scarborough doubles in 2026.

item.title: Make the Ankara Summit About European Defense Autonomy
item.description: As NATO meets in Ankara amid transatlantic strain, European allies must present the Trump administration with a burden-shifting roadmap, put its defense industry on a wartime footing, and advance NATO-EU cooperation by addressing Turkey’s role in European defense.

item.title: Saudi Vision 2030 at Ten
item.description: Ten years after its launch, Vision 2030 remains Saudi Arabia's roadmap for resilience. The Iran war reinforced—not weakened—the case for economic diversification, with AI, digital infrastructure, and strategic adaptation now central to the kingdom's long-term ambitions.

item.title: Is the Industrial Base on a Wartime Footing? A Progress Report
item.description: Is the U.S. defense industrial base on a wartime footing? This analysis measures the Pentagon’s progress toward this goal across key categories, including defense spending, new entrants, munitions, rare earths, and foreign military sales, and identifies where gaps remain.

item.title: What Does NATO Defense Spending Look Like Heading into the Ankara Summit?
item.description: As NATO allies meet in Ankara this week, defense spending will likely be on the agenda. Seamus Daniels outlines recent trends as NATO commits to increased spending.

item.title: How the Iran War Weighs on the U.S.-Saudi Partnership and Prospects for Normalization with Israel
item.description: Saudi Arabia neither sought nor engaged in the Iran war, yet it was forced to manage its consequences. The conflict has reinforced Riyadh’s determination to reduce regional instability while avoiding entanglement in crises beyond its control.

item.title: Russian Attitudes Are Shifting as the War’s Effects Come Home
item.description: Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian refineries combine military and economic pressure in ways previous shocks did not. While unlikely to transform public opinion, they raise the Kremlin's domestic costs and create an opportunity for the West to amplify the pressure.

item.title: China’s SLBM Test Underscores the Importance of a Ballistic Missile Launch Notification Agreement
item.description: On July 6, 2026, China conducted a submarine-launched ballistic missile test into the Pacific, its first ever into international waters. The insufficient notification underscores the importance of the Hague Code of Conduct.

item.title: Export Nation or Ecosystem Power: South Korea’s Choice in the AI Industrial Age
item.description: Navin Girishankar argues South Korea's second "Miracle on the Han River" hinges on becoming an ecosystem power—fusing capital, standards, tech, and know-how for the AI age.

item.title: The Geography of Coercion: Russian Missile and Drone Campaigns in Ukraine
item.description: How does Russia decide where to strike? This analysis maps the evolving geography of Russian missile and drone attacks, revealing how Moscow targets Ukraine’s military, infrastructure, and cities to maximize coercive pressure.
